title: Akhenaten tribute at the Hale Solar Laboratory
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Akhenaten tribute at the Hale Solar Laboratory, about 1920s at Hale Solar Laboratory, Pasadena, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: When he designed the Hale Solar Laboratory in Pasadena, he included a tribute to Akhenaten in the arch above the entrance,

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the astronomer George Ellery Hale built his own sun observatory, the Hale Solar Laboratory in Pasadena, California, in the 1920s. According to Michels, Hale put a tribute to Akhenaten, an ancient Egyptian king known for worshipping the sun, in the arch over the entrance. Michels raises it as a sign that old religious ideas sit quietly underneath modern American space science.
